summary: Agriculture innovation money is flowing to tools that cut input costs on existing farms: Deere's camera sprayers (5 million acres in 2025), biological fertilizers, and gene editing now that the EU has passed light-touch rules and the US approved a PRRS-resistant pig. Venture money has fled lab-grown meat and vertical farms after billions in losses. The farm equipment cycle is at a bottom in 2026, so tech adoption is coming from retrofits and pay-per-acre models, not new machine sales. Corteva completed its split on Oct 1, 2026: seeds and gene editing now trade as Vylor (VYLR), while crop protection and biologicals stay in Corteva (CTVA). Fertilizer stayed costly through the Hormuz disruption (US retail urea about $655 a ton in early September 2026), which keeps the cost case for nitrogen-fixing microbes alive.

innovations.name: Precision and autonomous farming
innovations.what: Cameras, GPS and AI on tractors and sprayers that spray only the weeds, plant at the right depth, and drive themselves for jobs like tillage. Farmers increasingly pay per acre instead of buying new machines.
innovations.stage_why: Deere's See and Spray covered about 5 million acres in 2025 with roughly half the herbicide, and autonomous tillage passed 200,000 acres. That is still a small share of US cropland, and the equipment downturn slows new purchases.

evidence.cost: See and Spray cut herbicide use by about 50% on 5 million acres in 2025. Deere prices autonomy kits low and charges per acre.
evidence.money: Deere sells autonomy retrofit kits for 2022 and newer 9R and 2020.5 and newer 8R tractors. Kubota partnered with Agtonomy for autonomous specialty crop tractors. Monarch Tractor raised about $220 million to $242 million, then laid off nearly all staff in early 2026.
evidence.revenue: AGCO's PTx precision business was about $860 million in 2025, guided flat to modestly up in 2026. Deere earned $1.379 billion in fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended Aug 2) on sales up 5% to $12.608 billion and raised fiscal 2026 net income guidance to $4.75 to $5.0 billion, but Production and Precision Ag sales fell on lower volumes in Brazil and Europe. See and Spray Gen 2 (model year 2027) adds variable rate dosing and speeds up to 16 mph.

spreads_to.use: Lower herbicide volume per acre; chemical makers shift to targeted products.
Same autonomy and guidance kits used on earthmoving and haul equipment.
Rural connectivity (satellite links) needed for machines to stream data.

innovations.bottleneck: The installed base and dealer network. Deere, CNH and AGCO control the machines and the data they produce, and retrofits must fit their tractors.

next_milestone.event: Deere fiscal Q4 2026 results and fiscal 2027 outlook, including precision tech adoption

innovations.thesis_broken_if: See and Spray and autonomy acres stop growing in 2026 to 2027 even as the equipment cycle recovers.

innovations.name: Gene edited crops and livestock
innovations.what: Using CRISPR to make small, precise changes to plants and animals, such as disease-resistant corn or pigs immune to a costly virus. Unlike older GMOs, many edits add no foreign DNA, so rules are lighter.
innovations.stage_why: The rules have just opened up (EU law adopted June 2026, US PRRS pig approved 2025), but most big products launch from 2027 to 2029, and the pig needs export market approvals before wide US sales.

evidence.approvals: EU Regulation 2026/1388 on new genomic techniques adopted June 17, 2026, applying from July 17, 2028; simple edits treated like conventional plants. FDA approved PIC's PRRS-resistant pig gene edit April 30, 2025; Canada approved it Jan 23, 2026, and Brazil, Colombia and the Dominican Republic have also cleared it; Mexico has no framework for gene edited animals yet and Japan is still reviewing. US SECURE rule was vacated in December 2024; USDA listed an interim rule for 2026 and asked for public input on future biotech rules on May 15, 2026.
evidence.money: Inari raised $144 million (cumulative $720 million). Corteva's seed business, including its plan for gene edited disease-resistant corn in 2028, was spun off as Vylor (NYSE: VYLR) on Oct 1, 2026.
evidence.revenue: Little so far. Cibus targets a 2027 Latin America rice launch and pushed its US launch to 2029. Genus says it will not sell PRRS-resistant pigs in the US or Canada until Mexico and Japan approve, so US revenue has slipped past 2026.

spreads_to.use: Lower disease losses and more uniform crops and animals cut processor costs.
Disease-resistant animals reduce vaccine and drug use.
Shared CRISPR tools, patents and licensing with human gene editing.

innovations.bottleneck: Germplasm and regulatory approvals. Vylor (the former Corteva seed unit) and Bayer own most elite seed genetics, and Genus owns the leading pig genetics; edits only pay when added to these lines and approved in export markets.

next_milestone.event: Mexico and Japan approvals for the PRRS-resistant pig (needed before any US sales); USDA interim biotech rule

innovations.thesis_broken_if: China or Mexico rejects edited pork imports, or the EU law is delayed or narrowed before it applies in 2028.

innovations.name: Alternative and cultivated protein
innovations.what: Meat and dairy substitutes made from plants, from microbes in fermentation tanks, or from animal cells grown in steel tanks. The newer focus is fermentation-made ingredients like whey and egg proteins.
innovations.stage_why: Plant-based meat reached stores years ago but is shrinking, cultivated meat has five US clearances but tiny volumes and seven-plus state bans, and fermentation proteins are only now reaching first commercial deliveries.

evidence.cost: Whey protein concentrate rose from $1.52 a pound in January 2026 to as high as $2.18 in July, which improves the economics for fermentation-made dairy protein.
evidence.approvals: Five cultivated products cleared in the US (Upside, Good Meat, Wildtype salmon, Mission Barns pork fat, Believer). Believer shut down in December 2025. Texas became the seventh state to ban cultivated meat (effective September 1, 2025, expiring September 2027).
evidence.money: GFI: alternative protein investment fell to $881 million in 2025 from $1.1 billion in 2024; fermentation $357 million (down 43%), cultivated $74 million (down 48%). ADM and Rich's backed Every Co. fermented egg protein (2026).
evidence.revenue: US plant-based meat retail sales fell 10% to $1 billion in 2025. Beyond Meat Q2 2026 revenue $68.8 million, down 8.2%, with $323.8 million debt. Perfect Day plans first ProFerm deliveries from its India plant with Zydus in Q4 2026 to Q1 2027.

spreads_to.use: Protein drinks and bars for GLP-1 users and fitness buyers.
Fermentation plants and know-how overlap with biologic drug manufacturing.
Cultivated and fermented proteins approved for pet food first in some markets.

innovations.bottleneck: Fermentation tank capacity at food-grade cost, and cheap feedstock sugar. Few large bioreactor sites exist outside pharma, and cultivated meat also lacks cheap growth media.

next_milestone.event: Perfect Day first commercial ProFerm deliveries

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Whey prices fall back and fermentation protein still cannot match them on cost by 2027, or more states ban cultivated meat.

innovations.name: Vertical and controlled environment farming
innovations.what: Growing greens, berries and tomatoes indoors under LED lights or in high-tech greenhouses, close to cities and year round.
innovations.stage_why: Most well funded vertical farms failed: Plenty, Bowery, AppHarvest and AeroFarms lost investors about $2.7 billion. Survivors focus on premium crops like strawberries or on greenhouses, so this is a stalled pilot, not a growth market.

evidence.cost: Electricity and capital costs remain above field farming for most crops; Local Bounti carries about $303 million of senior debt against about $54 million of annualized revenue.
evidence.money: Oishii (premium strawberries) closed a first $150 million of a Series C in May 2026, led by SPARX. Venture money for leafy-greens vertical farms has largely stopped.
evidence.revenue: Local Bounti revenue grew 15% in early 2026 but it received an NYSE listing notice in February 2026 and needed last-minute financing. Plenty filed Chapter 11 in March 2025 after raising about $940 million.

spreads_to.use: Greenhouses converted to cannabis and plant-made medicines (Village Farms converted 550,000 square feet).
Horticulture LEDs and climate control sold to greenhouses.
Grocers want local, steady supply of berries and greens.

innovations.bottleneck: Cheap power and cheap capital. Without low electricity prices and low interest rates, few crops pay back, which is why money now favors greenhouses and premium berries.

next_milestone.event: Local Bounti NYSE compliance and refinancing outcome; Oishii Series C final close

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Already partly broken: if Oishii and the greenhouse operators also fail to reach profit by 2027, the category stays a niche.

innovations.name: Ag biologicals
innovations.what: Microbes, enzymes and natural compounds that feed or protect crops, for example soil bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air so farmers buy less fertilizer.
innovations.stage_why: Products are on millions of acres and the leading supplier is growing 7% to 8% a year, but biologicals are still a small share of the fertilizer and chemical bill and results vary by field.

evidence.cost: Nitrogen is the cost biologicals attack: US retail urea averaged about $655 a ton in early September 2026 (DTN) after Hormuz disruptions, while global urea eased to $443 a ton on Sep 4 as China resumed exports.
evidence.approvals: Pivot Bio launched CERT-N, described as the first gene edited nitrogen-fixing product for cotton.
evidence.money: Novonesis launched a EUR 1 billion share buyback and signed Rovensa Next to distribute its plant health biologicals in the US. Pivot Bio has raised about $618 million across seven rounds (Tracxn), with a $2 billion valuation set in 2021; its third generation corn product, PROVEN G3, is due commercially in 2026.
evidence.revenue: Novonesis H1 2026 organic sales growth 8%, full-year guide raised to 7% to 8% with 37% to 38% EBITDA margin. Pivot Bio passed $100 million in revenue and 5 million acres in fiscal 2023, its latest disclosed figures. Corteva crop protection volume rose on demand for new products and biologicals.

spreads_to.use: Replaces part of synthetic nitrogen and some pesticides.
Same microbes and enzymes used in food fermentation and baking.
Lower fertilizer use can earn carbon and sustainability credits for growers and food brands.

innovations.bottleneck: Proven field performance and distribution. Microbe strain libraries are held by Novonesis, Corteva, Bayer and startups, and farmers buy through ag retailers like Nutrien that choose which products to push.

next_milestone.event: First quarterly report from the new crop protection only Corteva (biologicals growth disclosed separately from seeds for the first time)

innovations.thesis_broken_if: Biological sales growth falls to the low single digits in 2027 while fertilizer prices are high, which would show farmers do not trust the results.
